title: delegation_tokens: verify over received wire bytes, not re-encoded claims (same pattern as lquv)
description: Noted in project-LICHEN-worker6-lquv: python/src/lichen/crypto/delegation_tokens.py verify_delegation_token has the same re-encode-then-verify pattern local_facts.py had — from_cose_sign1 discards received protected/payload bstrs and verification rebuilds them via to_cbor()/cose_protected_header(). RFC 9052 4.4 signs bstrs AS TRANSPORTED; a fact/token validly signed by a C/Rust encoder with different map-key order, non-minimal int, or extra protected entry decodes fine but verifies False (Python<->C/Rust interop break). Fix mirrors the lquv change: retain received protected/payload on the token during decode, verify over those bytes, re-emit them verbatim in to_cose_sign1. Check the other COSE modules too (capability_announcements, key_rotation_attestation, root_dio_signature) — tunnel_auth.py:256 and handoff.py already use the retain-wire-bstrs pattern and are the model.
close_reason: Fixed across all 4 COSE modules: delegation_tokens (DelegationToken + PrefixDelegationToken), capability_announcements, key_rotation_attestation, root_dio_signature. Each envelope dataclass retains protected_bytes/payload_bytes on from_cose_sign1 (via dataclasses.replace, re-runs __post_init__ pair check) and on create_*; verify_* builds Sig_structure over transported bstrs per RFC 9052 4.4 with re-encode fallback for field-constructed objects; to_cose_sign1 re-emits retained bytes verbatim. 5 new independent-oracle tests (foreign map order + extra protected entry, signed via schnorr48 directly); all 5 confirmed RED pre-fix, GREEN post-fix. 766/766 crypto+local-fact tests pass (was 761; +5 new). 3x reviewer codereview: correctness PASS, security PASS; edge pass filed 3 beads: codebase-wide payload/wire desync (comment on existing 2vp1), to_cose_sign1 kid-vs-retained-payload encode inconsistency (P3), dataclass __eq__ change (P4).
